subject.title: fix(zalo): add timeouts to Bot API requests

question: Should the Zalo client impose the shared 30-second default deadline on every ordinary Bot API operation, or should deadline policy remain operation-specific beyond the existing explicit long-poll and media cases?
rationale: The mechanical duplicate-identifier defect is clear, but the compatibility tradeoff of a universal ordinary-request deadline is a channel behavior policy that code inspection alone cannot settle.

options.title: Adopt the universal default
options.body: After repairing compilation and refreshing exact-head proof, accept 30 seconds as the documented default deadline for all ordinary Zalo Bot API calls.

options.title: Keep operation-specific deadlines
options.body: Limit defaults to documented or empirically bounded operations and leave other ordinary calls without a new universal deadline until their contract is established.

recommendation.title: Adopt the universal default
recommendation.body: After repairing compilation and refreshing exact-head proof, accept 30 seconds as the documented default deadline for all ordinary Zalo Bot API calls.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on Zalo abort and polling behavior makes this the closest evidence-backed routing candidate, though ownership confidence is limited.
